title: POC: deployment pathway & benchmark sprint - Archipelago Health
summary: Intro POC scoping to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on success criteria (latency, cost, throughput), workload sizing for clinical NLP pipeline, benchmark plan (synthetic + replay), and 4-week sprint timeline. Key concerns: PHI handling, KMS integration, audit logs, and on-prem networking. Consensus: start hosted pilot with strict data controls, run benchmark suite, then evaluate Dedicated if throughput/cost require it; Private only if regulator requires on-prem.
topics: deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sara O'Neill (Archipelago Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, align on POC objectives: 1) validate latency at 95th < 250ms for short-text clinical extraction; 2) throughput target 120-200 QPS for batched workloads; 3) cost per 1k tokens target to meet budget; 4) security gating for PHI. Plan: run hosted pilot with anonymized replay, run bench suite, then decide if Dedicated is needed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick run through goals for the poc and then get into sizing and benchmarks. you should all have the one-pager link i sent, uh if not i'll drop again in the notes

00:31 Speaker 2 (Sara): yeah got it, thanks. real quick — high level, our use case is clinical note classification and entity extraction, very sensitive PHI, avg request size is 350 tokens, but there are spikes to 1k sometimes, and latency matters for triage flows.

01:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): great, that's helpful. do you have 7 days of representative trace logs or a sample? that helps us build a replay for benchmarks

01:18 Speaker 2 (Sara): we can provide a sanitized sample. marcus will handle the export. note we'll need proof of encryption at rest and customer-managed keys ideally (KMS/HSM)

01:37 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yep i'll pull a redacted subset. on the infra side we have a VPC in us-east-1 and strict egress rules, so peering or private link will be needed. we also have FISMA-ish controls but not full fedramp, and SOC 2 is a must.

02:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): timeline wise we're targeting a pilot in mid-october, three to four weeks, with go/no-go at the end. success means meeting latency and cost thresholds and sign-off from security.

02:34 Speaker 2 (Liam): okay cool. to scope, i want to walk through the three deployment modes and how they map to your constraints: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and is easiest for running initial benchmarks; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower variance; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for customers that require full network isolation or regulatory restrictions.

03:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): and important tradeoffs — hosted has flexibility and quick setup, but if your sustained QPS is high Dedicated often reduces unit cost; Private adds ops lead time and tends to push timeline out by 4-8 weeks depending on on-prem work.

03:37 Speaker 2 (Sara): do you have ballpark unit costs for hosted vs dedicated for transformer models? even rough is ok, we need to compare to our cost target of $0.50 per 1k tokens processed after optimization

04:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): rough guidance: hosted optimized path typically lands around $0.60-0.9 per 1k tokens for small- to mid-size models under moderate volume; Dedicated can drop that to $0.25-0.5 depending on batching, quantization and cache hit rates. but real numbers depend on your request mix and sequence length.

04:32 Speaker 3 (Marcus): and what about latency? our triage UI needs 95th < 250ms for short prompts — is that achievable on hosted?

04:48 Speaker 2 (Liam): short answers: yes for many models with streaming disabled and with prefix caching; but 95th at 250ms is tight, depends on model size, sequence length, and whether you can accept a smaller quantized variant. we'll test during the benchmark.

05:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): let's capture success criteria explicitly: latency 95th <250ms for 99% of triage queries? wait — 95th, not 99th — agreed? cost threshold $0.50 per 1k tokens after optimizations, throughput baseline 120 QPS sustained, and security controls (SOC2, KMS) validated. is that a fair starting point?

05:44 Speaker 2 (Sara): yes that's fine. also need audit logs for every request and token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback purposes.

06:03 Speaker 3 (Marcus): also note we have occasional batch jobs transferring entire day's notes for reprocessing overnight — heavy throughput but latency not critical there. so we might use different modes for online vs batch.

06:28 Speaker 2 (Liam): exactly, that's a common pattern — hosted for quick online prototyping, dedicated for heavy sustained batch or latency SLOs, private only if regulatory prohibits cloud-hosted PHI.

06:52 Speaker 4 (Priya): hypothetically if we hit cost targets in hosted but fail latency, do you support hybrid where inference routes to dedicated for high-priority routes?

07:06 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes — Redwood supports smart routing and policy-based fallbacks. you can pin critical endpoints to dedicated pools and less critical flows to hosted, and the platform will route by policy.

07:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): for the POC we're proposing: 1) you send a sanitized 7-day sample, 2) Redwood runs a hosted benchmark replay (48 hours) with our benchmark harness, 3) we produce a report with latency and cost profiles and suggested config (batching, quantization, cache settings), 4) if results look off we schedule a dedicated-run follow-up.

07:56 Speaker 2 (Sara): timing? if we give you logs by Friday can you run the replay that week?

08:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we can kick off a smoke within 48 hours of receiving data — full 48h run likely next week.

08:12 Speaker 2 (Marcus): network-wise we'll need to validate VPC peering or private link for the hosted pilot, is that automatically supported?

08:24 Speaker 2 (Liam): hosted can support VPC peering or private link for traffic egress, we also offer a no-ingress model where only outbound traffic to Redwood endpoints is allowed and no data is persisted beyond the session if you choose. we'll share the network checklist.

08:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): security ask list: SOC 2 cert, encryption at rest + in transit, customer-managed KMS recommended, audit log retention options. we'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC 2 report link.

09:00 Speaker 2 (Priya): you mentioned customer-managed KMS — do you integrate with AWS KMS and HSM providers?

09:08 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes we integrate with AWS KMS and support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments; for hosted we can offer CMK bring-your-own-key patterns in some regions — we'll confirm the exact support matrix in the security docs.

09:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok next let's talk benchmarks and metrics we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (QPS), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, KV/prefix cache hit rates, memory footprint, and model dropout/fallback events.

09:58 Speaker 2 (Sara): for our triage path we care about cold-starts too — occasional model cold starts happen when weights are swapped for quantized variants. can you measure warm vs cold separately?

10:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): yep we'll include cold-start tails. we'll also instrument latency by token position so you can see decoder vs encoder costs.

10:39 Speaker 3 (Marcus): about load shape — our peaks are bursty around morning rounds (8-10am) with short spikes to 180-200 QPS for 30 minutes. sustained is about 50-80 QPS. does your hosted autoscaling handle that?

11:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): hosted autoscaling does handle burst, but the key is the SLO for queueing; if the burst pattern is frequent Dedicated with reserved pools can give more predictable latency. part of the benchmark is to replay the morning spike and see 95th behavior.

11:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): also worth noting we have an Optimize toolkit that suggests batching and cache settings based on trace distribution — we'll try recommended profiles during the second pass of the benchmark.

11:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): question on data residency — some of our data originates in eu-west-1. do you have hosted regions there?

11:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes we have hosted regions in EU and NA; for private deployments we can deploy to customer region as required. we'll mark eu-west as a requirement in the security doc.

12:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): for the replay harness what's the expected format? we can export S3 objects with timestamped requests and response stubs.

12:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): good — we'd prefer newline-delimited JSON with fields: request_id, timestamp, prompt, metadata. we'll send an example and a small script to scrub PHI if you want.

12:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): small note on costs: if you go Dedicated you commit to reserved capacity; we'll show committed vs burst pricing in the pilot proposal.

12:51 Speaker 2 (Sara): what's a realistic ramp in the pilot? we can't risk production, so the pilot should be test-only — no live traffic.

13:01 Speaker 1 (Maya): agreed — pilot will be isolated, replay-only, and we'll control endpoints so nothing hits production UI. after sign-off we can talk about canary traffic for real-time validation.

13:14 Speaker 3 (Marcus): potential red flags for us: inability to use our KMS model, unacceptably high audit log latency, or network setup causing data leakage concerns.

13:29 Speaker 2 (Liam): on instrumentation we will provide per-request request-id mapping and a trace that you can cross-check with your logs; we'll also support Syslog/CloudWatch exports for audit events.

13:47 Speaker 1 (Maya): next — timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) collect sanitized traces and network details; Week 1 run hosted smoke (48h) + report; Week 2 run tuned replay with Optimize suggestions; Week 3 review and decision. that fits your mid-Oct target?

14:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): that seems OK, assuming Marcus can get the traces out by Friday.

14:13 Speaker 2 (Marcus): i'll aim for Friday EOD. need to check with security on scrubbing rules first.

14:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. i'll send the security whitepaper, network checklist, and the benchmark harness repo link. we'll also include sample pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated.

14:34 Speaker 2 (Sara): can you also show model variants — e.g., 7B quantized vs 13B fp16 — and the expected perf tradeoffs?

14:45 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes we'll include models and recommended quantization profiles and a tradeoff table in the report.

15:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): any other questions?

15:06 Speaker 4 (Priya): not from me. high level seems good.

15:10 Speaker 2 (Marcus): no more questions. thanks.

15:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok recap and next steps — action items listed in the notes: sara/marcus to share sanitized logs and network diagram; may and liam to run smoke and prepare benchmark report; maya to send contractual template and security docs. we'll reconvene after the Week 1 report, propose a 30-minute follow-up deep-dive.

15:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and dates. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions (speaker labels generic), some words may be mistranscribed (e.g. KMS->K M S, quantize->quantity), filler words present.
